document.title: Usama bin Ladin: Pakistan Seems to Be Leaning Against Being Helpful (Islamabad 09215)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan's Bin Laden Policy
document.note: [Secret] After the Clinton-Sharif meeting, the Embassy concludes the Government of Pakistan is not disposed to be especially helpful on bin Ladin. Pakistani sources say bin Ladin is a problem the U.S. has with the Taliban, not with Pakistan. It cites a journalist with ISI connections saying Pakistan wants nothing to do with the anti-Osama crusade. The Embassy will keep trying but calls it an uphill slog. Excised.

key_claims: The US Embassy judged Pakistan disinclined to be helpful on Usama bin Ladin two weeks after Sharif's US visit.
Pakistan took the line that Bin Ladin is a US-Taliban problem, not a Pakistani one.
The embassy attributed Pakistani reluctance to a history of negative public reaction to turning terrorists over to the US.
The Pakistani establishment was reportedly surprised at the vigor of the press and public reaction to a possible extra- or semi-legal rendition.
Zehra argues the Taliban will not hand over Bin Ladin and only military or clandestine means would remove him, which Pakistan publicly condemns as interference.
Zehra argues Pakistan wants good relations with all Muslim states and Islamic movements and should stay away from the US anti-Osama crusade.
